rival_compete_entry.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_entry.text: The courtyard had been rearranged without ceremony. Cord hung between short posts; covered trays rested beneath the loggia; three stools faced a rail whose wood had never been near the kiln mouth. Lin took the stool with a loose rung, tested it once, and exchanged it before anyone called the movement a trial. Across the yard, a woman in cinnabar watched the exchange with a small, unguarded frown.

rival_compete_intro_002.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_intro_002.text: You gave the chair more time than the course. Qiu Lian said it without smiling, as if stating a sum she expected Lin to contest. Her charcoal sleeves ended above practical boots, and her single black braid lay between narrow shoulders. The bright robe made her look ceremonial until she turned a tray with the blunt side of her hand. Every movement arrived where she had meant it to arrive.

rival_compete_intro_003.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_intro_003.text: The course hasn't begun. The chair would have stayed under me. Lin set the unsound stool against the wall, outside the walking lane. She could have added that her shoulder disliked sudden catches. Instead she sat with both feet grounded and let the arm rest across her lap. Her limits were already part of the agreed trial; she need not offer them as a plea whenever someone noticed her.

rival_compete_intro_004.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_intro_004.text: Three afternoons, three questions. Su Yao laid a small wooden bell beside the water jar. We will compare methods on low loads, with the ordinary stops we agreed. Nobody touches hot equipment. Lin remains behind this cold rail. Qiu may walk the cord course, but she will carry only its empty tags. If you disagree about a result, keep the disagreement. A public trial can survive two accounts.

rival_compete_intro_005.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_intro_005.text: Su's ivory and teal sleeves had acquired a flour mark at one cuff. The mark made her seem less like a steward presiding over rivals than someone interrupted while doing useful work. She brushed it once and left what remained. Behind her, two neighbors stood under the loggia, a boy swung his heels from the low wall, and an old woman held her own cup. None had been invited to chant anyone's name.

rival_compete_intro_006.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_intro_006.text: I asked for the comparison because people remember the longest explanation. Qiu touched a brass pointer, then took her finger away before it moved. A quick accurate reading vanishes into the next task. A slow recovery produces a story. I would like speed to get a fair hearing. I do not mean rushing an injured arm, and I don't want that sentence turned into the thing people say I came here to prove.

rival_compete_intro_007.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_intro_007.text: Then ask for speed by its proper name. Lin looked at the covered trays rather than at the spectators. I want a person who inherits our result to know what can be recovered when something slips. If that makes every sound reading slower, you should be allowed to show it. If your quick reading cannot be checked after a mistake, I should be allowed to show that. We can leave the descriptions open until the objects answer.

rival_compete_intro_008.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_intro_008.text: Qiu lifted her chin a fraction. The answer had neither welcomed nor dismissed her challenge. A rival could be a person who prevented an easy account from closing too soon. Lin had known competition that treated care as embarrassment, and care that secretly required everyone else to be worse. She did not want either arrangement. The yard gave her an easier task: look at the cord, listen to the bell, and answer what was actually asked.

rival_compete_intro_009.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_intro_009.text: The facility grant is twenty-four copper, held by the steward for agreed facility costs. Su pointed toward a closed expense pouch on her side of the rail. It is not either participant's purse. Neither participant receives a prize or wages. You are spending time you chose to make available. If a bell ends an afternoon before an answer appears, we keep the unfinished question rather than buy another hour with somebody's obligation.

rival_compete_intro_010.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_intro_010.text: Good. Qiu's relief was so immediate that Lin almost missed it. I don't want a patron placing a purse between us, then explaining which woman deserves it. Let the objects be ungrateful. She checked the cord posts by sight, walking the outside line without leaning over the rail. At the fourth post she stopped. This knot has been dressed differently. Is that part of the test, or did someone put a thumb through it?

rival_compete_intro_011.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_intro_011.text: Preparation, Su said. The course is not ready for scoring yet. I will reset the knot before I cover its tags. You may inspect the bare arrangement now, because both of you can inspect it. She brought the post within Lin's view by rotating its base, rather than asking Lin to stand and reach. Qiu watched that adjustment with an expression Lin could not read. The steward did not ask anyone to praise the courtesy.

rival_compete_intro_012.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_intro_012.text: The cord carried twelve numbered places and four loose tags. The tags weighed less than a spoon, yet the arrangement imitated a common nuisance: a reading traveled through several hands while its starting point stayed behind. From the rail, Lin could see all twelve places but could not touch them. Qiu would do the placing. Su would change one harmless connection during each run. They would be testing messages, not strength, and mistakes would remain visible.

rival_compete_intro_013.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_intro_013.text: I can carry four positions in memory without writing each turn. Qiu tapped her temple once with a knuckle. I can also read them aloud. These are different costs. If you make me repeat every position merely because repetition sounds solemn, the comparison has been decided before the bell. Tell me what information you need back. I will give it quickly, and we can discover whether quick is enough rather than pretending it is an insult.

rival_compete_intro_014.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_intro_014.text: An origin, an order and a place to restart. Lin traced three short strokes on her own slate with her sound hand. She did not draw a map of every peg. More is possible, but those are the questions I would ask if the cord arrived in my lap already wrong. Which end began the count, which way did the count proceed, and what survives if we lose our place? I don't yet know the cheapest answer.

rival_compete_intro_015.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_intro_015.text: A neighbor named Pei asked whether both women had the same cultivation stage. Su answered that they worked within the same bounded fifth stage, with four pairs, and that the trial would not examine a realm or award advancement. Qiu rolled her eyes at the question without looking at Pei. Lin understood the impatience. A stage could describe a capacity while leaving all twelve pegs unmapped. It would be comforting to make one title do the work of a dozen observations.

rival_compete_intro_016.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_intro_016.text: If my method wins one course, I am not asking you to abandon your method everywhere. Qiu turned back toward Lin. But I am asking you not to say it won only because the course was easy. Ease can be useful evidence. The things we do often ought sometimes to be easy. She spoke the last sentence more softly. Lin heard experience behind it but had no warrant to invent the experience. She kept her attention on the words.

rival_compete_intro_017.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_intro_017.text: And if mine wins a changed course, you don't have to call the change sabotage. Lin rubbed a grain of chalk off the slate's edge. A fair disturbance is still a disturbance. We can say your method was faster while the course stayed sound and slower after it changed. We can also say my precautions were wasted if no disturbance mattered. I want a description that keeps both costs, even when I like one result better.

rival_compete_intro_018.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_intro_018.text: The boy on the wall ceased swinging his heels. He had apparently expected a contest in which someone stumbled and the other person laughed. Qiu noticed him watching, picked up an empty tag, and turned it twice between two fingers. She could have made a little display of dexterity. Instead she placed it flat where Lin could see its number. The restraint made her more formidable. She was choosing what the spectators would have to notice.

rival_compete_intro_019.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_intro_019.text: There are three ways to frame the first run, Su said. You may lead with the clock and accept a narrow account. You may lead with recovery markers and accept their time. Or you may exchange roles in the explanation: Qiu handles the cord while Lin gives a compact instruction that another person could repeat. Each framing gets the same agreed afternoon interval. We cannot fit all three into this afternoon, so choose the question you want answered.

rival_compete_intro_020.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_intro_020.text: Lin felt the familiar temptation to select the method most likely to vindicate her. Nothing in the invitation forbade that choice. Still, vindication purchased by a narrow question could leave her less informed at the end. Qiu had brought a challenge that might expose a habit, and a habit was more valuable than a moment's applause. The bell waited beside Su's hand. Across the rail, Qiu folded her charcoal sleeves evenly and said nothing while Lin considered the course.

rival_compete_intro_021.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_intro_021.text: I will follow the framing you choose, Qiu said at last. This is your chance to make the comparison answer a real doubt. Don't choose my strongest ground merely to look generous. Don't choose yours merely to look prudent. If you want to know whether I can beat the clock, give me the clock. If you want to know whether I can leave a recoverable error, give me the error. The answer might irritate both of us.

rival_compete_intro_022.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_intro_022.text: I don't promise to enjoy losing. Lin's voice came out drier than she intended, and Qiu finally smiled. I can promise not to move the marks afterward. She checked the position of her arm against the stool back, took a drink, and set the cup on the lower shelf. These small movements would remain outside the timed course. Su had made their separation clear. Lin did not need to win comfort as a concession from an opponent.

rival_compete_intro_023.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_intro_023.text: The courtyard noises continued around them. Someone rinsed a bowl beyond the gate. A cart wheel clicked over a stone, paused, then clicked again. The trial occupied a small part of the town's afternoon, and that proportion steadied Lin. Whatever happened, people would still want supper and the cracked stool would still need mending. Qiu followed the wheel's sound with her eyes, then looked back at the twelve pegs as though the world had given her an efficient reminder.

rival_compete_intro_024.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_intro_024.text: Before you choose, look at the scoring card. Su held it against the cold rail. We record the number of correct final places, time to first answer, and time to a correction after the arranged change. There is no combined score. Combining them would require us to decide their importance before we know their cost. You may disagree later about which measure deserves priority. You may not erase an inconvenient measure because the other two suit you.

rival_compete_intro_025.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_intro_025.text: The card had three columns and no space for a winner's flourish. Lin liked it at once, which made her wary of calling it neutral. Qiu studied the same card, then asked Su to add the number of unnecessary resets. A method could recover perfectly by restarting endlessly. Su added the fourth column for both participants. That request altered Lin's idea of her rival. Qiu was not simply impatient with checks; she wanted checks to answer for the labor they required.

rival_compete_intro_026.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_intro_026.text: And a false stop, Qiu said, is still a result. If I ring the bell over a harmless difference, write it down. If Lin does, write it down too. I would rather have a rival than a witness who politely keeps the mistakes belonging to my method off the page. She glanced toward the expense pouch, then away. We agreed this place could afford the trial, not that it could afford unlimited caution disguised as an absence of mistakes.

rival_compete_intro_027.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_intro_027.text: A missed stop goes beside it. Lin waited until Su had written the phrase. There was satisfaction in this disagreement: they were making room for one another's preferred objections. It was also slightly frightening. She could already imagine her own habit filling the false-stop column. She could imagine Qiu's speed leaving a missed change. Neither possibility told her what would actually happen. The course lay ready, and imagined embarrassments were still only imagined.

rival_compete_intro_028.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_intro_028.text: Su covered the tags with a narrow board. Qiu moved to the far end of the cord without stepping across the marked lane. Lin remained seated behind the cold rail, close enough to speak at an ordinary volume. The old woman under the loggia tucked her cup into her sleeve to keep its warmth. No one counted down. The first bell would sound only after the framing was selected, and the ordinary afternoon would then become a measured piece of it.

rival_compete_intro_029.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_intro_029.text: Choose one first-run framing, Su said. The clock-first trial tests whether a concise account can survive the arranged disturbance. The recovery-first trial tests whether visible restart marks justify their delay. The exchanged-instruction trial tests whether a fast hand and a recoverable message can work together without either woman quietly doing the other's thinking. All three are permitted. I will keep the other two questions for another occasion rather than claim we answered them today.

rival_compete_cord_choice.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_choice.text: Qiu's fingers rested open beside the first peg. Lin held the chalk without pressing it against the slate. Between them, the cord was a small visible thing that could bear none of their pride unless they chose to hang it there. Lin could choose a brisk contest, an explicit recovery test, or a shared instruction whose authorship would itself become difficult. The choice would shape this afternoon's evidence and the questions waiting on the next one.

choices.text: Lead with the clock: test Qiu's compact current account.
Lead with recovery markers: test an inherited sequence.
Exchange instructions: test fast hands and a recoverable message.

rival_compete_cord_fast_entry.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_fast_entry.text: Su lifted the cover and sounded the bell. Qiu moved along the posts as though she had already heard the order in the bare arrangement. First tag to the third peg, second tag across the return cord, third tag beside the start, fourth tag at the far post. She spoke each destination once. Lin wrote only the four numbers and a small arrow. By the time the boy resumed swinging his heels, Qiu had stepped clear.

rival_compete_cord_fast_002.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_fast_002.text: Read it back. Qiu did not ask whether Lin was ready; the agreed procedure allowed her to request the readback as soon as the last tag rested. Her eyes stayed on the cord rather than on the slate. Lin gave the numbers and the direction. Qiu corrected none of them. Su marked the first time, then turned the covered disturbance card. A quick clean beginning was now a fact, whatever the rest of the afternoon did to it.

rival_compete_cord_fast_003.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_fast_003.text: The first arranged change moved the start marker one post inward. It did not change the tags. Su made the movement openly and then folded her hands. Qiu glanced once at the new origin and delivered a revised sequence. Lin heard the four numbers with the same firm cadence as before. The third place sounded wrong. She checked her arrow, checked the visible marker, and asked Qiu to say only the third destination again. The clock continued running.

rival_compete_cord_fast_004.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_fast_004.text: Nine. Qiu's answer came immediately. She followed Lin's look, frowned, and amended it. Ten. I carried the old origin through that one. Her voice stayed ordinary, but the color high on her face deepened. Su wrote the first answer and its correction in separate cells. The spectators did not murmur. The quiet denied Qiu both an excuse and a humiliation. She had made a small recoverable error in a course that had initially suited her.

rival_compete_cord_fast_005.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_fast_005.text: I saw it because I kept the direction arrow. Lin laid the chalk down before adding anything else. I did not see the second number until you repeated the third. If both had shifted, my shorthand might have hidden it. She expected Qiu to argue about the imagined second error. Instead Qiu looked at the slate with interest. Their first mistake had given them a narrower useful question: what could this particular scrap of writing actually detect?

rival_compete_cord_fast_006.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_fast_006.text: They ran the unchanged sequence again. Qiu finished faster. Lin's four numbers took their place beside the earlier four without ceremony. When Su moved the start marker back, Qiu corrected every destination before speaking. The old woman under the loggia nodded once, approving either the speed or the evident correction. Lin could not tell which. She felt the first tug of competitiveness in her throat: she wanted the next disturbance to expose something her little arrow could repair.

rival_compete_cord_fast_007.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_fast_007.text: This run has no origin change, Su announced after the second clean answer. She turned a peg so its painted number faced the wall. The tag and peg stayed where they were. The physical place remained clear from Qiu's end, but from Lin's stool the number disappeared. This was within the advertised course. Qiu could see a thing Lin could not, and their quick message now had to carry more than a convenient shared view.

rival_compete_cord_fast_008.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_fast_008.text: Fourth from my right, Qiu said. Lin waited, and Qiu caught the problem before being prompted. Fourth from the far gate. Eight. She gave the relation, the anchor and the number in a single breath. Lin could have demanded the entire sequence again. She accepted the local correction and wrote an eight with a small square around it. Su marked no false stop. Qiu's mouth tightened in satisfaction at having repaired the message without restarting the course.

rival_compete_cord_fast_009.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_fast_009.text: The next tray contained tags whose ink looked similar in the afternoon glare. Qiu placed a six where a nine belonged. The error was not a failure to count; she had read the mark upside down as her hand turned it. Lin's arrow offered no help. She read the slate back perfectly, reproducing the wrong tag. Su let the run finish, then lifted both tags together. A fast agreement had carried an error that neither participant's preferred safeguard had caught.

rival_compete_cord_fast_010.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_fast_010.text: That one belongs to both of us. Lin said it before Qiu could claim or reject responsibility. I repeated what you supplied without asking whether the mark had an orientation. If the purpose was merely to preserve your message, I did that. If the purpose was to preserve the tag's identity, we failed. She pushed the slate toward the rail, keeping it on her own side. A repeated reading could sound reassuring while proving only that two people remembered the same mistake.

rival_compete_cord_fast_011.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_fast_011.text: I can make the top visible with one turn. Qiu aligned the tags toward the gate. That costs less than asking four questions after every run. She waited for Lin's response instead of carrying straight on. Lin nodded. They agreed that orientation would be part of the starting arrangement from the next run onward; it would not rewrite the failed run. Qiu placed the six and nine correctly this time, and the ordinary correction was quicker than the discussion that had named it.

rival_compete_cord_fast_012.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_fast_012.text: Three clear runs followed. Qiu's hands were not preternaturally swift. They were simply economical: she turned toward the next post while still finishing the present instruction, kept each tag flat, and avoided reaching back for things she could set in order once. Lin found herself admiring the craft despite her resolve to remain an opponent. Admiration did not cost her judgment. On the fourth run, she could still point out that Qiu had omitted the origin from the spoken account.

rival_compete_cord_fast_013.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_fast_013.text: It hasn't changed, Qiu answered. Then she looked at Su's still-covered card and exhaled. You can't know that until she uncovers it. She supplied the origin without a theatrical concession. The correction added two beats. Lin noticed that she had begun counting those beats against herself, as though a reasonable request were already a debt owed to the rival's efficiency. Su's clock gave the request a cost without telling her that the cost was shameful.

rival_compete_cord_fast_014.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_fast_014.text: A longer cord loop made the far side difficult to distinguish from the near side. Qiu's first answer remained correct, but Lin had to look twice before writing it. The delay belonged to Lin's comprehension, not to a misplaced tag. Qiu stood silent until the readback arrived. That silence was disciplined and uncomfortable. It offered Lin the time she needed while displaying, with perfect fairness, where the time had gone. She could not repair her pride by accusing Qiu of pressure.

rival_compete_cord_fast_015.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_fast_015.text: You can record that I was slow to distinguish the return line. Lin kept her eyes on the cord as she said it. The marks were sufficient; I did not use them promptly. She did not offer an elaborate history for the hesitation. Qiu inclined her head. In that brief acknowledgment, Lin felt a cleaner kind of rivalry than a contest over who could produce the longest account of why an unfavorable result did not belong to her.

rival_compete_cord_fast_016.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_fast_016.text: We have enough clean speed readings for the question we selected. Su lifted the bell but did not sound it. The remaining time permits one longer disturbance, not three. I can separate a cord, obscure the starting marker, or change a tag order after the first answer. The clock-first framing has already produced useful evidence. You may choose which weakness to inspect next, but that choice will not turn the other two disturbances into observed successes.

rival_compete_cord_fast_017.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_fast_017.text: Qiu looked at the separated-cord card first. Lin noticed the look and resisted making a decision solely to oppose it. She wanted a disturbance that would test the bargain they had actually made: minimum writing, rapid movement, local correction when possible. She asked Su to change the order after the answer, keeping the origin visible. Qiu agreed. This left their useful arrow intact while attacking the sequence both women had been treating as stable.

rival_compete_cord_fast_018.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_fast_018.text: Su exchanged the middle two tags after Qiu stepped clear. Qiu saw the hand movement and gave the new order instantly. Lin crossed out the middle numbers, but her crossed lines touched the last number as well. When she read back, she hesitated over what she herself had written. The slate had become the slow object. Qiu waited without satisfaction. Su timed the delay until Lin replaced the whole four-number line with a clean one.

rival_compete_cord_fast_019.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_fast_019.text: Your first arrow saved my origin mistake, Qiu said. Your later crossings made my correction harder to receive. I don't think either fact cancels the other. She crouched beside the low post, well outside Lin's rail, and rested one wrist on her knee. I expected you to make me slow down. I didn't expect the paper, or the slate, to become the thing slowing both of us after I had already corrected the cord.

rival_compete_cord_fast_020.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_fast_020.text: I expected the slate to remain simpler than the course. Lin could hear how absurd that expectation sounded once spoken. It was still true that she had held it. She wiped the crossed line only after Su copied its state. Recoverability included the receiver's surface, not just the sender's sequence. This was not a new calling bestowed by an afternoon. It was an awkward observation she could use the next time a quick correction arrived on a messy page.

rival_compete_cord_fast_021.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_fast_021.text: The final scored run used clean writing and Qiu's compact orientation cue. The first answer was correct and quick. The arranged change displaced one middle tag; the correction was also correct, though Lin took longer to replace her line than Qiu took to speak it. Their initial error remained in the earlier column. Su did not make the clean ending swallow it. Qiu had won the separate clean-message timing comparison with Jian. The recoverability question had yielded a mixed account rather than a rescued victory for Lin.

rival_compete_cord_fast_022.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_fast_022.text: I want the fast readings left visible, Qiu said. Not because they excuse the six and nine, but because we did not spend all afternoon making that mistake. Lin agreed. She could see a version of the story in which her own correction became the memorable event and Qiu's dozen efficient movements became mere prelude. That version would be pleasing and dishonest. Qiu's insistence asked Lin to treat successful ordinary work as evidence with a claim on memory.

rival_compete_cord_fast_023.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_fast_023.text: Under the loggia, Pei asked who had won. Qiu began to answer, stopped, and looked toward Lin. Lin pointed to the matched-message timing row and named Qiu. She pointed to the moved-origin correction and named the usefulness of the arrow. She pointed to the swapped marks and said both women had failed them once. Pei looked disappointed by the shape of the answer. The boy on the wall looked relieved, as though complexity had saved him from choosing whom to cheer.

rival_compete_cord_fast_024.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_fast_024.text: Your economy held up better than I expected. Lin said it to Qiu directly after the spectators turned toward the water jar. I still want a cleaner restart surface. I also want to stop pretending that every extra word I add is automatically a safeguard. Qiu did not smile at the concession. She listened closely enough that Lin had to finish the thought without escaping into humor. Some of my words merely make me feel less exposed.

rival_compete_cord_safe_entry.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_safe_entry.text: Lin chose visible restart marks. Su brought a second slate to the rail and gave Qiu three thin ribbons for the course. A ribbon marked the origin, another marked the return, and the third marked the last place whose identity both participants had confirmed. Qiu examined them without pretending to be delighted. The ribbons added objects to manage before the bell. Lin wanted to know whether their usefulness would exceed that addition, and the clock would preserve the answer.

rival_compete_cord_safe_002.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_safe_002.text: I'll set them where your view stays clear, Qiu said. She turned the third ribbon outward rather than leaving its knot behind the post. Then she stopped and looked back. That turn cost time. Keep it. Lin nodded. Qiu was drawing attention to labor that courtesy often hid. Making information available to a seated receiver was ordinary work, even when nobody thought to name it. The slower beginning would include the work instead of charging it to Qiu's supposed reluctance.

rival_compete_cord_safe_003.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_safe_003.text: At the bell, Qiu placed the four tags in order and paused at each agreed checkpoint. Lin read the positions back in pairs, drawing a short upright stroke beside each confirmed pair. The first answer was correct. Each confirmation added a measurable pause before the final answer. The old woman under the loggia shifted her cup from one hand to the other. Qiu stood beside the final ribbon and waited for Lin to decide whether the delay had bought anything yet.

rival_compete_cord_safe_004.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_safe_004.text: A sound course doesn't prove the marks useful. Lin disliked hearing her preferred arrangement reduced to that sentence. She said it anyway. We have paid for a capacity we have not needed. Su wrote the first answer time without adding an approving comment. Qiu reached for the first ribbon, then stopped because the reset had not been called. Her discipline made the delay more visible: this was not a slow participant accidentally lengthening a sound method.

rival_compete_cord_safe_005.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_safe_005.text: Su changed the origin after the first answer. Qiu saw the movement and reached toward the first tag. Lin asked her to hold, identified the last confirmed pair on the slate, and gave a new starting relation. The ribbon made the old relation visible beside the new one. Qiu moved two tags instead of four. Their corrected answer was slower than Qiu's imagined instant repair, but the slate still showed exactly where the earlier answer had ceased to apply.

rival_compete_cord_safe_006.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_safe_006.text: I would have changed those two without the ribbons, Qiu said. She spoke calmly, making the objection harder to dismiss as wounded pride. Lin agreed that she probably could have. The actual evidence was narrower: a person reading their slate now could see the old origin and the point of replacement. Qiu looked toward the spectators. You have a better inherited account. We haven't shown you a better first correction. Those ought to have different names on the card.

rival_compete_cord_safe_007.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_safe_007.text: Inherited account, Su repeated, and added a note below the columns. It will remain a note unless we test a new reader. We cannot turn every good description into a scored result simply by wanting one. She asked Pei to leave the loggia briefly while the next course was set. Pei protested that he would miss the interesting part. That is the point, Su said. If you see the arrangement being made, you are not inheriting the account.

rival_compete_cord_safe_008.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_safe_008.text: Pei returned after the disturbance and stood at the far end where Qiu had stood. The tags had been covered; only Lin's slate and the ribbons remained visible. Su asked him to reconstruct the last valid sequence without moving a post. He found the first pair, hesitated at the origin change, then followed Lin's replacement line. Qiu supplied no hints. His answer was correct, slower than either woman's, and entirely dependent on marks she had resented arranging.

rival_compete_cord_safe_009.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_safe_009.text: That is useful, Qiu said before anyone prompted her. Pei beamed as though she had praised his skill rather than their evidence. Qiu let the misunderstanding stand until he moved away. Then she turned to Lin. But I gave you a consistent hand through the entire change. A ribbon placed badly can make this method look sound while adding a fresh wrong anchor. I want one disturbance to the markers themselves. Otherwise your safety objects have escaped the test.

rival_compete_cord_safe_010.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_safe_010.text: Su loosened the last-confirmed ribbon and tied it one peg farther on. She did so after both women looked away, in the prearranged interval for an unseen harmless disturbance. Qiu started the next run, stopped at the ribbon, and glanced at Lin for the readback. Lin gave the pair shown beside her upright stroke. The ribbon disagreed. She almost corrected her slate to match it before remembering that the slate represented a witnessed earlier placement.

rival_compete_cord_safe_011.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_safe_011.text: Hold the course. Lin's voice sounded sharper than the low-load trial needed. She lowered it on the next sentence. The ribbon and my last confirmation disagree. I cannot tell which moved from where I am. Qiu stood still, hand clear of the tags. Su recorded the stop, then asked Lin what observation would resolve it. Lin could inspect the earlier ink. Qiu could inspect the knot. Neither observation alone would identify the intended current pair.

rival_compete_cord_safe_012.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_safe_012.text: The knot is loose and its dust line doesn't match the peg. Qiu pointed without touching. That tells us the ribbon moved. It doesn't tell us where you meant it to rest. She had a clean answer to part of the question and declined to stretch it into the whole. Lin looked at her with reluctant gratitude. A less careful rival could have restored the course at once and left Lin praising an apparent recovery that depended on Qiu's private memory.

rival_compete_cord_safe_013.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_safe_013.text: They reset from the origin rather than guess the lost marker. The choice sacrificed a substantial portion of the remaining trial time. Lin's method had preserved the disagreement but had not preserved enough independent evidence to make the repair local. Su wrote the reset in the fourth column. Qiu did not need to say that the column had been her suggestion. Its dark stroke was already speaking on her behalf, and Lin could feel her own enthusiasm for ribbons growing less uncomplicated.

rival_compete_cord_safe_014.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_safe_014.text: A second reader reconstructed one altered sequence. One damaged marker required a full restart. Su read the notes aloud so neither participant could summarize only the part she liked. There remains time to compare a shorter marker scheme. You may remove one ribbon now if both agree. You may also keep all three and spend the time on another disturbed run. The first arrangement remains recorded either way. Revision is possible; invisibility is not.

rival_compete_cord_safe_015.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_safe_015.text: Lin proposed removing the last-confirmed ribbon and using the slate's pair marks as their sole confirmation record. Qiu studied the far posts, then asked what would happen if Lin's chalk line blurred. Lin answered that they would have to stop and resolve the record, just as they had stopped over the ribbon. Qiu nodded. She accepted a vulnerable object that had been honestly named. What she resisted was a object whose designation as a safeguard made its own failures impolite to mention.

rival_compete_cord_safe_016.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_safe_016.text: Let the ribbon mark only the origin and the turn. Qiu untied the third strip and put it on Su's table, without pocketing it or treating it as waste. Then every object has one job. If you need to restart, you won't have to decide whether this little cloth means the last good pair, the next pair, or the pair I happened to stand beside. The simplification sounded so obvious that Lin felt a brief irritation at not having proposed it herself.

rival_compete_cord_safe_017.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_safe_017.text: The shorter arrangement still began slowly. Lin read pairs, Qiu paused, and Su kept the clock. When the turn marker was shifted, the pair strokes isolated the disagreement quickly. Qiu moved one tag, gave the relation from the origin, and waited for Lin's confirmation. The correction time improved. It remained longer than a quick private correction might have taken. Their result was not the discovery that care could be free; it was the discovery that one of their careful objects had been needlessly ambiguous.

rival_compete_cord_safe_018.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_safe_018.text: I like having less to defend. Lin said it with a tired laugh, and Qiu answered with a small one of her own. Removing the ribbon had made Lin's method feel more exposed, but the exposed parts could be named. She could now explain which marks survived a moved turn and which did not survive a blurred line. Qiu's economy had entered the recoverability method as a correction rather than as an enemy trying to abolish it.

rival_compete_cord_safe_019.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_safe_019.text: The final blind disturbance came while Lin rested her hand and looked at the water jar. Su replaced a tag with another bearing the same visible number but a different notch. Qiu read the number correctly. Lin confirmed it correctly. The number-based account preserved everything they had chosen to preserve and lost the notch. When Su uncovered the paired tags, Lin stared at the distinction. No amount of repetition could recover a detail they had never decided to record.

rival_compete_cord_safe_020.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_safe_020.text: I saw the notch, Qiu admitted. I didn't call it because our question was the numbered place. If you now say it proves I should have spoken more, I will ask which other details you wanted. The grain? The string color? The scratch on the edge? She was not evading the missed distinction. She was demanding a boundary around completeness. Lin looked at her own careful slate and recognized how easily a record could claim more fidelity than it had ever attempted.

rival_compete_cord_safe_021.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_safe_021.text: It proves we should say what the record covers. Lin turned the slate toward Su. Number, place, direction, confirmed pairs. No shape identity beyond the number. If the inherited task later needs the notch, this record cannot supply it. She did not add notches to the last trial retroactively. The omission hurt precisely because the method had worked well within its selected bounds. A successful record could invite a future reader to trust it in a way its makers had never tested.

rival_compete_cord_safe_022.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_safe_022.text: Pei returned to reconstruct the final changed sequence. This time Su told him that the record did not establish tag identity by shape. Pei asked why anyone would care about the notch. Qiu held the two tags side by side and said that someone might, on another task. He reconstructed the numbered arrangement correctly, then left the notched tag question blank. His blank was less satisfying than a complete answer and more faithful to the evidence he actually possessed.

rival_compete_cord_safe_023.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_safe_023.text: The recovery framing produced a readable inherited sequence and caught a moved turn. Su set the clock down. It also spent time on confirmation, required a full restart when one marker became untrustworthy, and preserved no unrecorded shape detail. These are the results we observed. Qiu's compact first-answer method was not separately timed under these selected disturbances. We should not borrow a victory from a question we did not choose.

rival_compete_cord_safe_024.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_safe_024.text: I lost patience before the first bell. Qiu looked at the folded third ribbon. That was not a measured result, but it was mine. I thought you wanted three ribbons because three sounds safer than two. One of them did. The other two had distinct work. She paused, then lifted her eyes to Lin. I will not call the whole arrangement fuss after watching Pei recover the changed turn. I may still call the first version fussy.

rival_compete_cord_safe_025.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_safe_025.text: Call it by the version, Lin answered. First version, three ribbons, one ambiguity, one inherited success. Second version, two ribbons, clearer boundaries, time still spent. She had lost the hope of presenting recoverability as a virtue that needed no rival's objections. In exchange she possessed a smaller claim she could stand behind. Qiu's judgment no longer felt like a threat to the account. It felt like part of the labor that kept the account from becoming a flattering story.

rival_compete_cord_safe_026.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_safe_026.text: They left the third ribbon on Su's table with the failed arrangement sketched beside it. The spectators could inspect both versions while the women drank water behind the cold rail. Lin's shoulder remained quiet; the strain she felt was in the attention she had paid to being publicly wrong. Qiu sipped from her own cup and watched a neighbor study the extra ribbon. Neither woman moved to explain first. For a moment the objects were allowed to make their own slow introduction.

rival_compete_cord_pair_entry.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_pair_entry.text: For the exchanged-instruction framing, Qiu took the tags and Lin took a blank slate. Lin would write the shortest directions she believed recoverable; Qiu would follow them without adding an unspoken interpretation. Su would ask a second reader to use the directions after the disturbance. The arrangement sounded cooperative until Lin realized how readily each woman could hide behind the other's error. A poor instruction could look like a poor execution. A clever executor could make a poor instruction appear sound.

rival_compete_cord_pair_002.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_pair_002.text: I will do what you wrote, Qiu said. If I know a quicker route, I will keep it to myself until this run ends. If I do not know what a phrase means, I will ask before moving that tag. She held the first tag at waist height so Lin could see its top edge. This will be slower than being left alone with the cord. You have selected the meaning of a message, so let us give the message an honest chance to fail.

rival_compete_cord_pair_003.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_pair_003.text: Start from the gate-side peg. Move the first tag three numbered places toward the wall. Lin read the sentence aloud while writing it. She had meant to be concise, yet each relation sprouted another possible question. Did numbered places include the peg where the tag began? Did toward the wall follow the upper cord or the return? She added those two answers, then stopped. If every instruction anticipated every imagined doubt, the afternoon would end before Qiu could place anything.

rival_compete_cord_pair_004.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_pair_004.text: Qiu performed the first movement correctly and quickly. At the second sentence she halted. Lin had written take the next tag across. Across had an obvious meaning to Lin because she could see both cords at once. From Qiu's end, two plausible crossings lay beside her hand. Qiu asked for a destination number. Lin supplied it, and Su marked the interruption. The first correction belonged to the instruction. Qiu had refused the opportunity to choose a sensible meaning privately and let Lin's phrase escape inspection.

rival_compete_cord_pair_005.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_pair_005.text: I could have guessed the intended peg, Qiu said after the run. Guessing well is sometimes part of skill. Today it would have hidden your missing destination. She placed the slate upright against Su's table instead of handing it back immediately. From this end, she added, your next tag is also not obvious. It could mean the one next in the written order, the one beside my hand, or the one left after the move I just finished.

rival_compete_cord_pair_006.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_pair_006.text: Lin rewrote the instruction using tag numbers. The revision shortened one sentence and lengthened another. She could feel the appeal of Qiu's brisk questions: they stopped her from filling every ambiguity with a blanket of extra language. The next run went cleanly until Su shifted the origin. Qiu completed the first pair from the old origin because the slate did not state whether its starting peg was a physical place or the marker that might move. Lin watched her own intention fail to travel.

rival_compete_cord_pair_007.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_pair_007.text: That is my omission. Lin said it before Su asked. I meant the marker. I wrote a place. She wanted to add that the choice had been obvious before Su moved it. That addition would merely describe why she had overlooked the distinction. Qiu nodded and waited. Lin changed the phrase to marked origin and kept the original sentence beneath it, crossed once but legible. Two versions now showed the difference between what she believed she had said and what she had actually said.

rival_compete_cord_pair_008.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_pair_008.text: The second reader was the old woman with the warm cup, whose name was Jian. She set the cup on the wall and read Lin's amended directions with a patient squint. Qiu held the tags ready. Jian interpreted the first two sentences correctly, then paused at count forward. Forward depended on the reader's body. Lin heard the gap as soon as Jian said it. A direction that survived one careful executor had still failed to survive a new pair of feet.

rival_compete_cord_pair_009.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_pair_009.text: Gate to wall, Qiu said, then looked at Su. That is advice outside the instruction. Record it separately. Jian smiled as though advice itself were welcome whether scored or not. She completed the course after the correction. The arrangement was accurate, and it had taken a long time. Lin's compact message was becoming less compact with each ordinary human perspective. Qiu's speed was not disappearing; it was waiting for the message to stop asking her to repair meanings invisibly.

rival_compete_cord_pair_010.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_pair_010.text: Exchange now, Su said. Qiu will draft the instruction; Lin will call it from behind the rail, and Jian will move the tags. No carrying or reaching is required from Lin. This reverses authorship, not the physical limit. Qiu took the slate and wrote four lines quickly. Lin could not see the lettering until Qiu laid it on the rail. The hand was neat and narrow. Every line named a tag, a destination and a visible anchor. There were no ornamental assurances.

rival_compete_cord_pair_011.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_pair_011.text: Lin read Qiu's first sentence without difficulty. Jian placed the tag correctly. The second sentence used an arrow instead of a word, and Lin read the arrow from her own side rather than from Qiu's writing side. Jian followed the spoken direction into the wrong return loop. Su sounded the soft stop bell before the next movement. Qiu stared at the slate, then turned it a quarter turn and frowned. A wonderfully economical symbol had quietly assumed an orientation nobody had agreed.

rival_compete_cord_pair_012.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_pair_012.text: Mine, Qiu said. Then she caught herself. The arrow's mine. The spoken direction is Lin's, but the slate gave her no fixed top. We don't need to split the blame like a loaf. She drew a small gate mark at the top edge. This makes the arrow's view explicit. Lin appreciated both the correction and the refusal to turn responsibility into a contest for larger shares. They needed to identify what to change, not establish who could endure the most public self-accusation.

rival_compete_cord_pair_013.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_pair_013.text: After the fixed top was added, Qiu's instructions became markedly quicker to read than Lin's first version. Jian followed two clean courses without questions. Lin's own voice grew steadier as the relations stayed consistent. Qiu watched the sequence rather than enjoying the comparison visibly. She had won a useful point: compact instructions could remain recoverable if their anchors were well chosen. Lin could accept that point without pretending her earlier fuller phrasing had anticipated it.

rival_compete_cord_pair_014.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_pair_014.text: Your four lines carry more than my first six did. Lin kept the slate level on the rail. I think I was adding words where I hadn't chosen an anchor. Qiu studied the original crossed sentences before answering. Some words were doing work, she said. Count forward wasn't. She did not dismiss the whole draft, and Lin noticed how much easier that made revision. A rival who could discriminate between defects was harder to resent than a rival who condemned everything indiscriminately.

rival_compete_cord_pair_015.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_pair_015.text: Su next removed the gate-side marker and placed a blank post where it had been. The physical gate remained visible. Lin read Qiu's directions from the fixed-top slate. Jian reached the correct first place, then asked whether the missing mark canceled the authority of the gate drawing. The question was cautious but legitimate: the message had named both a permanent object and a removable mark. Qiu had reduced several ambiguities and created a smaller one at their intersection.

rival_compete_cord_pair_016.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_pair_016.text: Use the gate, Qiu said. The mark was a convenience, not the origin's authority. Lin looked down at the slate. It did not say that. Qiu followed her look and was silent for a moment. Then she added a brief line: origin is gate-side post, even if marker is absent. The addition made the instruction longer. She wrote it with an air of someone paying a fair bill she had hoped would not arrive.

rival_compete_cord_pair_017.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_pair_017.text: They debated whether a permanent gate could itself become a weak anchor if the course moved to another yard. Su let the debate continue for three breaths, then asked which course they were testing. The courtyard course, Lin said. Qiu nodded. Their recovered instruction did not need to become a universal treatise on all gates. It needed an explicit limit. Lin wrote courtyard course along the bottom edge. Qiu smiled at the placement, as if relieved that a boundary could be shorter than an attempted cure for everything.

rival_compete_cord_pair_018.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_pair_018.text: There is time for one inherited correction. Su asked Jian to step beneath the loggia while she changed the order of the middle tags. Qiu revised the instruction in Lin's view. Lin would explain the revision to Jian, and Jian would finish from the last confirmed pair. Both women could now see how tempting it was to provide a complete new performance instead of a message whose origin and revision another person could follow.

rival_compete_cord_pair_019.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_pair_019.text: Lin told Jian that the first pair remained valid and the middle order had changed. She showed the old line, the replacement and the fixed top. Jian moved one tag correctly and set the other on the old destination. Qiu opened her mouth, then closed it. The revised arrow lay too close to the old arrow. Jian had followed a real mark on a page they had intended to make obsolete. Su stopped the course with both arrangements still visible.

rival_compete_cord_pair_020.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_pair_020.text: We kept the old line readable but did not make its status clear. Lin heard the echo of her own preference for preserving failed evidence. Preservation and instruction were not the same surface. Qiu asked for a separate scrap. They copied the current directions cleanly and labeled the first slate as the earlier version. The old evidence stayed available on Su's table. Jian received a current instruction without having to solve the authors' correction marks as part of the course.

rival_compete_cord_pair_021.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_pair_021.text: The new scrap let Jian finish correctly from the confirmed pair. It cost time to produce and prevented an error that had already occurred once. Su recorded both facts. Qiu's four-line draft had supplied the strongest compact form; Lin's insistence on retaining versions had supplied a useful inherited account. Their first combined surface had muddled those purposes. Cooperation had not fused two methods into an effortless superior whole. It had created a new object with a failure belonging to both authors.

rival_compete_cord_pair_022.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_pair_022.text: I don't want this described as me moving while you thought, Qiu said while Jian returned to her cup. Nor as you writing while I knew the practical part. We both chose meanings. We both missed meanings. Lin answered before the sentence could harden into another dispute. Agreed. Qiu's shoulders lowered. What she feared was not merely losing a contest. It was being assigned the smaller kind of mind because her hands arrived at an answer first.

rival_compete_cord_pair_023.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_pair_023.text: Lin looked at Qiu's braid, the fine flour of chalk along her fingers, and the set of her mouth. She had known the rival for one afternoon. That was enough to see a concern and too little to write its origin. The boundary felt useful. She could answer the concern directly without composing a biography that would make Qiu's objection easier to categorize. She slid the current instruction toward the rail and asked whether Qiu wanted her name beside its four core lines.

rival_compete_cord_pair_024.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_pair_024.text: We can name the drafts by who wrote them and the final correction by who changed it. Lin tapped the separate surfaces. That leaves your concise anchors visible and my version history visible. It also leaves our muddled amendment visible. Qiu nodded once. She accepted authorship without claiming every useful element. Su added the names in her own hand, and the division of credit ceased to be a private favor the women could later remember differently.

rival_compete_cord_pair_025.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_pair_025.text: The exchanged-instruction afternoon ended with a correct inherited correction, a slow first draft from Lin, a faster anchored draft from Qiu, and a shared amendment that had caused one wrong placement. There was no single time to crown. The final scrap belonged to the facility trial rather than to either woman's purse or portfolio. Su laid it beside the earlier slates. The boy on the wall asked to copy the gate drawing, and Qiu showed him which side of the page must stay up.

rival_compete_cord_after_001.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_after_001.text: The first bell's quiet afterlife lasted longer than its sound. Su laid the timing card beside the failed objects, and the spectators drifted toward supper without agreeing on a winner. Qiu remained at the table, looking at marks that had embarrassed her as carefully as marks that favored her. Lin rested her arm, waited for the small ache of sustained posture to ease, and watched a sparrow investigate the abandoned stool. An afternoon could end without an account becoming final.

rival_compete_cord_after_002.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_after_002.text: Tomorrow's trays are covered now, Su said. Their covers will stay tied until both of you are present. The trial question changes from carrying a sequence to reading instruments whose identities you cannot see. You may bring a preferred test, but you will choose only one framing for the time available. She put the bell into a cloth bag. It disappeared like any household object, depriving the rivals of the little symbol that had made their disagreement seem official.

rival_compete_cord_after_003.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_after_003.text: I was angrier than I expected to be, Qiu said as they walked along the loggia's outer edge. Not when an object went wrong. When a useful part of my work was about to disappear inside somebody else's explanation. Lin stayed behind the cold side of the rail until Su opened the ordinary exit. She did not rush the walk to keep pace. Qiu noticed the difference and slowed without offering a story about why the slower pace had become noble.

rival_compete_cord_after_004.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_after_004.text: I can make an explanation eat a result. Lin looked at the courtyard rather than at Qiu. I know how to put an inconvenient number between two sensible sentences until it feels less inconvenient. I don't always notice I'm doing it. Qiu's answer was immediate. I can make speed eat a question. Then both women laughed, briefly and without intimacy. The symmetry was pleasant; neither wanted to let it become another comforting method of erasing what differed between them.

rival_compete_cord_after_005.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_after_005.text: At the shared kitchen, Su found a pot of plain barley tea and asked before pouring three cups. No one had ordered a victory meal. A neighbor had left enough tea for whoever remained at the facility, and the stewards' expenses would cover the water and charcoal already used. Lin's purse stayed closed. Qiu set her cup near a nick in the table, examined the nick as though it were another possible origin, then shook her head at herself.

rival_compete_cord_after_006.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_after_006.text: You may tell me to stop measuring the table. Qiu rubbed her brow. I sometimes keep the contest going after the objects have been put away. It makes me poor company for a cup of tea. Lin answered that she was still composing an explanation of the afternoon in her head, so neither woman could claim to have arrived fully at the kitchen. Su drank first. That ordinary movement gave them a better example than an instruction to relax would have done.

rival_compete_cord_after_007.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_after_007.text: The steam rose between them and thinned. They spoke about the broken stool, the boy's borrowed drawing, and whether the kitchen's ginger jar was empty. These matters did not deepen their rivalry; they gave it a human circumference. Qiu had a dry, practical joke about jars whose labels outlived their contents. Lin answered with a story about a cup repaired so often that its owner called every unbroken cup suspicious. Neither story required an earlier profession or a special right to tell it.

rival_compete_cord_after_008.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_after_008.text: I will keep today's chosen framing on tomorrow's card, Su said. The blinded readings will not begin from a claim that the cord answered everything. It answered one selected question. When I remind you of that question, you may disagree about its implications. She looked from one woman to the other. I expect disagreement. I also expect you to distinguish what you observed from what you now hope the observation means. Tea does not make that distinction unnecessary.

rival_compete_cord_after_009.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_after_009.text: The next afternoon arrived with a thin, cool rain. Lin checked the stool at the cold rail and found its rung secured by a new crosspiece. Su said the repair had been paid from facility upkeep, not from either participant's reward, because neither had a reward. Qiu ran a finger over the joint and asked whether it had dried fully. The repairer, standing under the loggia, answered without offense. Lin sat only after the ordinary question received an ordinary answer.

rival_compete_cord_after_010.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_after_010.text: Before the covers come off, remember what yesterday actually tested. Su placed the selected timing card on top of the new tray. The weather has changed and the instruments have changed. Your habits are coming with you, but the previous result must keep its original question. I will read the note from the framing you chose. Then we will let it sharpen the next question rather than declare either method the answer in advance.

rival_compete_cord_recall.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_cord_recall.text: Under the new covers, pointers clicked softly as the tray settled on the table. Qiu had stopped glancing toward the spectators. Lin noticed that the quieter second afternoon felt more demanding, not less. A single success could be carried into the next day like a charm, and a single loss could be carried like a grievance. The saved framing on Su's card gave both temptations a particular shape. They would have to hear it again before touching the new question.

rival_compete_cord_fast_cb_001.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_fast_cb_001.text: Yesterday you chose clock-first movement. Qiu's cards gave Jian quicker first placements in two matched clean comparisons; her direct-handling runs were timed separately. The moved origin exposed one carried-forward number. Lin's small arrow helped with that correction; her crossed slate later delayed a changed order. The six-and-nine mistake passed through both women. This afternoon does not begin with a general victory for either speed or recovery. It begins with a particular concern about how two people can confidently preserve the same wrong reading.

rival_compete_cord_fast_cb_002.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_fast_cb_002.text: I don't want to lose yesterday's useful economy merely because today's covers make us nervous. Qiu spoke directly to Lin. Give me an instrument that behaves cleanly and I still want to read it cleanly. But the six and nine showed me how quickly a wrong identity travels when the receiver trusts my orientation. I want the covers tied well enough that I cannot recognize a tray by a careless corner and call recognition a reading.

rival_compete_cord_fast_cb_003.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_fast_cb_003.text: My shorthand helped one change and obscured another. Lin left the old crossed slate where Su had put it. I won't bring it forward as proof that more writing solves the covered instruments. I want a record that another person can interpret after the cover comes off. Qiu nodded, then drew the new tray nearer the table's center without uncovering it. Their first day had left them more precise objections, and precision was a harsher gift than reassurance.

rival_compete_cord_safe_cb_001.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_safe_cb_001.text: Yesterday you chose visible restart marks. A second reader recovered a changed sequence; a shifted confirmation ribbon required a full restart; removing that ribbon made the later arrangement clearer. The record did not preserve tag shape, because you had selected numbers and places. This afternoon begins with the question of what a reading claims to identify. More marks do not supply a property nobody observed, and fewer marks do not automatically identify which property matters.

rival_compete_cord_safe_cb_002.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_safe_cb_002.text: I believed one of your ribbons was ornamental. Qiu looked at Lin rather than at the old table. One was ambiguous, two had work. I will try to keep that distinction when the instrument covers begin to irritate me. She tapped the covered tray with one knuckle, lightly enough not to move its pointer. I still want to know which checks justify their time. That is a question I can ask without pretending every check is the extra ribbon.

rival_compete_cord_safe_cb_003.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_safe_cb_003.text: I want the instrument record's limit written before we read it. Lin held the chalk loosely. Yesterday's notch mattered because a later reader might assume our number identified a whole tag. I don't want a covered pointer's position to turn into a claim about its spring, its age, or its fitness for a task we haven't tested. Qiu answered that those limits should fit on a useful page. The old disagreement had survived; its object had become more exact.

rival_compete_cord_pair_cb_001.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_cord_pair_cb_001.text: Yesterday you chose exchanged instructions. Lin's first draft needed new anchors; Qiu's shorter draft needed a fixed top; the shared amendment confused an inherited reader until current instructions were separated from older evidence. Each author's useful work and failed work remains named. This afternoon starts from the question of how a reading reaches another person. A good hand can conceal a weak message, and a clean message can transmit an observation whose source was never checked.

rival_compete_cord_pair_cb_002.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_cord_pair_cb_002.text: I liked the four clean lines better than the first crowded surface. Qiu nodded toward the retained drafts. I also liked keeping the failed surfaces available once they were no longer the instruction Jian had to follow. I want that distinction here. A covered result can be concise at the point of use while the evidence beside it stays long enough to inspect. She waited for Lin to answer rather than treating their combined draft as an agreement already covering every future tray.

rival_compete_cord_pair_cb_003.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_cord_pair_cb_003.text: I still hear Jian choosing the obsolete arrow. Lin smiled with discomfort at the memory. We can both know an instruction is superseded and fail to tell the next reader. Today I want the identity of the current reading clear, even if the old one stays visible for comparison. Qiu lifted the empty current-record board and set it in a separate space. The small separation did not solve the blinded trial, but it kept yesterday's particular lesson from becoming a vague compliment.

rival_compete_blind_scale_entry.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_blind_scale_entry.text: The direct-reference framing began with three covered instruments and one familiar brass weight. Su placed the weight where Lin could see its unaltered seal. No participant would lift more than the agreed small load; Qiu would handle the trays, and Lin would read the exposed pointers from the cold rail. The covers hid the makers' marks and repair scratches. They did not hide the scale faces. Qiu seemed pleased by the reduction: no story could tell them which instrument deserved trust.

rival_compete_blind_scale_002.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_blind_scale_002.text: One weight, same resting place, three readings. Qiu lined the trays beneath the loggia so the rain could not strike them. Let us answer the narrow question first: what does each face say under this weight? We can ask about return afterward if time allows. She looked toward Lin. A reading at one load is not a declaration that the whole scale is sound. If you see me drifting into that claim, stop me. I might like the clean answer too much.

rival_compete_blind_scale_003.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_blind_scale_003.text: Instrument A settled neatly on the expected mark. Instrument B rested a little high. Instrument C trembled between two marks before settling low. Qiu kept her fingers away from each pan after setting the weight. Lin called the positions aloud while Su copied them. The first sequence was quick and uncontested. The spectators could see three answers without seeing three identities, and their silence felt almost studious. Qiu completed the course before the kitchen door had stopped swinging from a passerby's departure.

rival_compete_blind_scale_004.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_blind_scale_004.text: A agrees at this load; B reads high; C took longer and reads low. Lin wrote the verbs carefully. She wanted to call A reliable, then withheld the word. Qiu glanced at the slate and nodded. The direct method had answered exactly what it claimed in a short time. Lin could sense her own desire to extend the question until her preferred recoverability work became necessary. She waited for Su to announce the planned disturbance rather than inventing a weakness to satisfy herself.

rival_compete_blind_scale_005.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_blind_scale_005.text: Su asked Qiu to remove the weight from all three instruments. A returned to its starting mark. B returned high, almost the same amount by which its loaded reading had been high. C returned slowly and stopped just short of its starting mark. Lin's initial note still distinguished the readings, but B's apparent loaded error now had a plausible different description: an offset face rather than an altered response. Qiu leaned closer without touching the tray, then stood back so Lin's view remained clear.

rival_compete_blind_scale_006.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_blind_scale_006.text: B's difference survives removal. Qiu pointed to the empty pan. Its response to the load may be closer to A's than the first positions suggested. We need the loaded change, not simply the printed mark. She had supplied the recovery observation that Lin had expected to have to demand. Lin added a separate column for empty position. The additional record cost little because Qiu had noticed precisely what mattered. A good rival could make her preferred objection arrive before she did.

rival_compete_blind_scale_007.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_blind_scale_007.text: They repeated A and B. A gave the same sound reading. B gave the same high position and returned to the same high empty position. Subtracting the empty position yielded the expected change under the reference weight. Su did not let that subtraction become a repair. B's face still needed its offset stated whenever used. Qiu described it as a stable offset at the tested load. Lin liked the specificity and disliked how difficult it was becoming to portray speed as careless.

rival_compete_blind_scale_008.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_blind_scale_008.text: The cover remains on B, Su said. You may infer a stable offset from these runs. You may not infer its cause or promise stability tomorrow. She moved a small screen so neither woman could glimpse the hidden maker's mark at an angle. Qiu accepted the limit without argument. Under the cover, B continued to be an instrument they had observed rather than one they knew by reputation. The trial's modesty made its good results stronger instead of making them trivial.

rival_compete_blind_scale_009.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_blind_scale_009.text: C behaved differently on the repeat. It rose past the mark it had reached before, trembled, and rested nearly where A had rested. Lin kept the two readings on separate lines. Qiu checked whether the weight had touched the pan's rim. It had not. The rain whispered along the outer tiles, and a drop struck the floor beyond the trays. C's inconsistency was now actual evidence; they no longer had to imagine it in order to justify a longer question.

rival_compete_blind_scale_010.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_blind_scale_010.text: I want to run C first next time. Qiu looked at Su. Perhaps settling time, perhaps the order of our handling. If it is drifting while we talk, another quick sequence might show less than waiting. She spoke that last word with a small rueful tilt of her mouth. Her efficiency method had not required perpetual haste. It required choosing what time could reveal. Lin agreed, surprised by how often their quarrel concerned useless time rather than all slow time.

rival_compete_blind_scale_011.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_blind_scale_011.text: They left C empty while Su turned the sandglass twice. No one filled the wait with a lecture. Qiu took a sip of water, Lin stretched the fingers of her sound hand, and Jian examined the bowl she had brought from home. The stopped work was visible, timed, and bounded. When Qiu placed the weight again, C gave its original low reading. The instrument's apparent improvement after repeated handling had vanished during rest. A single prompt reading could now mislead in either direction.

rival_compete_blind_scale_012.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_blind_scale_012.text: A reader who arrived after the second sequence might think C agreed with A. Lin pointed to the two lines. A reader who arrived after the rest might think it always read low. Neither line alone carries its behavior. She was glad to have an observation favoring history, then checked that feeling. The direct framing had produced the history by testing a repeat when the first answer differed. It had not proved that a long record was required before every ordinary first reading.

rival_compete_blind_scale_013.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_blind_scale_013.text: Qiu proposed one alternating run, C then A then C, to compare handling with a steady reference. Su allowed it within the remaining time. A stayed consistent between C's two different positions. The familiar weight had not changed enough to account for the movement. C's repeat behavior remained suspect. Lin wrote that the source of the variation was undetermined. An inconsistency could be caught without being explained, and an efficient account could preserve that unresolvedness if its author resisted the temptation to name a cause.

rival_compete_blind_scale_014.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_blind_scale_014.text: C loses the neat answer. Qiu's voice carried disappointment rather than anger. I wanted all three to settle into a useful classification quickly. A did. B nearly did, within a stated offset. C gives us a behavior question. She lifted the weight away and laid it in its shallow box. That is still a result. We have found which object deserves more time, instead of making all three spend the same time merely because one won't behave.

rival_compete_blind_scale_015.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_blind_scale_015.text: Lin could not dispute the economy. In her first imagined arrangement, every instrument would have received the same detailed cycle history. The chosen framing had produced a clear A, a bounded B and an unresolved C, concentrating its repeats where readings demanded them. Yet a short successful screen could become dangerous if later users converted its small labels into permanent assurances. She asked Su how the trial would preserve those distinctions when the covers were removed and people began recognizing familiar objects.

rival_compete_blind_scale_016.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_blind_scale_016.text: Each card stays with its tray until cleanup. Su held the blank tags ready. A: agrees at the tested load in these runs. B: repeated offset at empty and tested load. C: varied with repeat and rest, source undetermined. The names beneath the covers will be added below those statements, not in place of them. She glanced toward the spectators. Recognizing a maker is not permission to improve or worsen the observations you already made.

rival_compete_blind_scale_017.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_blind_scale_017.text: The covers came off. A was a scratched household scale with a plain wooden base. B had polished brasswork and a respected maker's stamp. C bore a small patch where an old support had been replaced. Pei immediately said he would have trusted B most. Qiu smiled without triumph. The blind trial had prevented the polished face from receiving a cleaner account than its actual positions. It had also prevented the humble A from being treated as a problem in need of explanation.

rival_compete_blind_scale_018.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_blind_scale_018.text: I recognized B's handle before the last cover came off, Qiu admitted. The screen hid its stamp, but the curve was familiar. I did not say so because recognition was not the chosen question. Su wrote the admission below the B card. Lin had not recognized it. Their blindness was therefore imperfect in different ways. Qiu's voluntary admission cost her a little of the clean narrative in which all three objects had been equally unknown, and made the surviving evidence easier to trust.

rival_compete_blind_scale_019.speaker: lin_yue
rival_compete_blind_scale_019.text: Does recognizing B change your recorded positions? Lin asked. Qiu said no. Does it change what you expected from them? Qiu answered yes, after a short pause. She had expected the high reading to be her own handling mistake at first. Lin could appreciate the difference. The numerical observations remained valid. The path by which Qiu decided to repeat the reading had been touched by reputation. A covered trial reduced one bias without making either participant a blank instrument.

rival_compete_blind_scale_020.speaker: narrator
rival_compete_blind_scale_020.text: They compared the faces openly for a final ordinary check. Qiu caught the reference weight against the rim of B's pan and corrected its placement before Lin called a number. Su wrote the handling interruption even though the final reading was sound. Qiu accepted that note readily. Her prompt method depended on skilled handling, and skilled handling could include stopping a slip before it became a recorded answer. The correction was real work, not evidence that no error had approached the process.

rival_compete_blind_scale_021.speaker: rival_su_yao
rival_compete_blind_scale_021.text: Today's direct framing produced a prompt valid initial set, with Qiu handling and Lin calling. Lin's separated repeat lines preserve C's changed behavior after handling and rest. The reference check identified a sound tested response, a repeated offset and an unresolved variable response. We have not tested other loads. We have not repaired B or C. Su's summary closed the possible claims before the spectators could enlarge them into either a triumph of polished craft or a condemnation of repaired objects.

rival_compete_blind_scale_022.speaker: rival_qiu_zhen
rival_compete_blind_scale_022.text: I would choose A for the same small load now, Qiu said. I would write the test date rather than call it always sound. I would keep B's offset visible. C should wait for a separate investigation. She looked at Lin. You may think that last recommendation gives recoverability the last word. I think it gives an unresolved instrument the time it actually earned. We need not call every sensible delay my defeat.

rival_compete_blind_scale_023.speaker: lin_yue
